impact.rationale: The patch adds default-off automated network fetch, machine authorization, durable scheduler state, and subscription candidate import. A defect can affect credential freshness, tenant/source isolation, replay safety, or persistent admission state.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: A deterministic source-visible CI regression exists: the patched legacy required-name producer observes 689 names while its workflow still requires 688. The new contract is also self-attesting and does not prove the claimed exact 700-name closure.

regressionProtection.rationale: The immutable patch contains 12 new top-level tests and a seven-package Linux Go job, but neither Go nor gofmt ran. The new checker validates only manifest self-consistency and subset membership, and the existing lifecycle workflow would reject the added authn top before Go.

recoverability.rationale: Refresh remains default-off and can be disabled or reverted, while its v2 sidecar is separately versioned. Once enabled it creates persistent scheduler and command/candidate records, so rollback requires preserving those records and cannot be treated as stateless.

confidence.rationale: Patch identity, all 27 afterimages, call paths, authorization, persistence, and checker behavior were inspected directly. Confidence is capped because Go compilation, gofmt, Linux tests, race tests, and runtime/network behavior were not executed.

applicability.rationale: The changed serverruntime path constructs the refresh store and SnapshotManager, configures the subscription service, and starts RunRefresh when the explicit refresh gate is enabled.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Without this patch automatic refresh remains unavailable and v1's replay and immutable-identity flaws remain unresolved, but the current default-off/manual path avoids introducing the new automated authority.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Only a current source-owned dedicated refresher principal with the exact grant set may execute automated refresh.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A disabled, expired, role-changed, scope-changed, copied, foreign, or stale principal reaches Fetch or Import.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: TrustedPrincipal obtains a process-bound reference; CurrentPrincipal rereads the secured file before Fetch and again before Import, exactRefreshPrincipal checks the sole role and exact grants, and RBAC is re-evaluated.

materialBoundaries.invariant: No binding change, deletion/re-addition, restart, or retry may reuse an earlier attempt or command identity.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: subscription RefreshStore and subscription Store ControlIdentity
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A changed schedule, approval, policy revision, or re-added binding resets attempt count and replays a prior command result.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Retained per-source generation, global LastSequence, full binding HMAC, sequence-bound attempt key, and one-time running recovery make identities monotonic; UNKNOWN has no next attempt.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Network content may be imported only under the same approved source/policy/revision and a fresh machine observation, and remains quarantined.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Policy material, approval, source revision, or identity changes during Fetch and stale content is admitted.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Approval and policy seal are checked before and after Fetch; fetched scope/source metadata is checked; identity and RBAC are reread immediately before Store.Import; the store enforces revision CAS and creates only a quarantined candidate. Identity observation and Import are explicitly adjacent but non-atomic.

materialBoundaries.invariant: HTTP callers cannot inject worker principal, resolver, URL, refresh authority, or automated command fields.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: API subscription decoder and subscriptionctl Command
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A client supplies Automated, approval age, SnapshotRef, URL, resolver, or identity fields in a POST body.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The API uses per-kind exact key sets and constructs Command fields manually; automated and SnapshotRef fields are not accepted by any write route, and refresh routes are GET-only.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Capacity exhaustion fails before network and never deletes admission, audit, command, or rollback history.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: RefreshOnce capacity gate and durable subscription stores
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A full command, candidate, or audit budget triggers a Fetch and then silently evicts old records or loses rollback history.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: RefreshOnce checks all three capacities before Fetch and records terminal store_limit; no archive or deletion exists. This is an acknowledged temporary fail-closed bound, not the future long-duration archive design.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Repository checks independently prove the old 688-name set plus exactly 12 new names, exact affected sources, and no undeclared tests.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: chengwang-subscription-refresh workflow and lifecycle source-contract workflow
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A change edits source_contract.json to omit an affected source or substitute names, or adds the authn test and trips the unchanged legacy 688 assertion.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The immutable artifact's patch has exactly 12 added Test functions and its actual old/new union is 700, but the committed checker only checks declared subset membership and manifest hashes supplied by the same mutable manifest.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The patch must not claim that the existing HTTP authenticator gains live identity-file revocation.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: serverruntime global identity Store and refresh-only SnapshotManager
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Operators rely on file replacement to revoke active HTTP identities without restart.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The delivery explicitly limits live reread to the refresh worker SnapshotManager and states the global HTTP Store remains immutable until restart.
